mappings.note: Identifies what is untrue of plantation farming; plantation is one of the cropping patterns LO-1 asks the candidate to classify. Not LO-2, which is about reforms.
Names the plantation crops: the 'major crops of India' half of LO-1.
Names the three cropping seasons: LO-1's cropping-pattern half in its purest form.
What rabi crops are: the rabi season within the cropping calendar, LO-1.
When and how kharif crops are grown: the kharif season of the cropping calendar, LO-1.
The main kharif food crop (rice): season-to-crop matching, LO-1.
The main rabi food crop (wheat): the rabi counterpart of qid:105948.
Names the zaid season between rabi and kharif: the third season of the cropping calendar, LO-1.
Names the major non-food crops: crop classification, LO-1.
The staple of eastern and southern India (rice): crop-to-region matching within LO-1.
The two wheat-growing regions: the geography of a major crop, LO-1.
Wheat's rainfall requirement: a growing condition of a major crop, LO-1.
The third most important food crop (millets): ranking within the major-crop classification, LO-1.
The leading bajra state: crop-to-state matching, LO-1. Not C-2.4, since no map work is required.
Growing conditions for maize: a major crop's requirements, LO-1.
Pulses as the chief vegetarian protein source: crop characteristics within LO-1.
What is untrue of pulses, including their nitrogen-fixing habit: crop characteristics, LO-1.
Ideal conditions for sugarcane: a major crop's requirements, LO-1.
Oilseeds' share of the cropped area: the crop mix, which is what a cropping pattern is, LO-1.
Conditions that spoil the tea crop: growing requirements of a plantation crop, LO-1.
Where coffee was first introduced in India: the origin of a named plantation crop, LO-1.
Rubber as the automobile industry's raw material: a major crop and its use, LO-1.
Names sericulture, the process of rearing silkworms. A term rather than a crop or a cropping pattern, so C-2.1 rather than LO-1; the fibre itself is asked separately at qid:106019.
Jute as the golden fibre: crop nomenclature within the major-crop list, LO-1.
Single crop over a large area is plantation agriculture: classification of a cropping pattern, LO-1.
Identifies a rabi crop: season-to-crop matching, LO-1.
Identifies a leguminous crop: crop classification, LO-1.

The minimum support price announced by the government is one of the three institutional supports LO-11 names explicitly. Not LO-13, which asks the candidate to relate policy to food security rather than identify the instrument.
Primitive subsistence farming as shifting cultivation: classification of a farming pattern, LO-1. Not LO-2, since no reform is assessed.
Plantation agriculture classed as commercial farming: placing one pattern inside another, LO-1.
The share of India's population engaged in agriculture is the workforce figure LO-12 is built on. Not LO-1, since no crop or pattern is at issue.
What cultivation methods depend on (physical environment, technology, socio-cultural practice). A general process statement, so C-2.1; LO-2 would require a specific reform to be assessed.
Farming ranging from subsistence to commercial: the classification axis itself, LO-1.
Identifies the pattern from its tools and labour (primitive subsistence): classification, LO-1.
What primitive farming depends on (monsoon and natural soil fertility): a defining feature of that pattern, LO-1.
Slash and burn identified as shifting cultivation: classification of the pattern, LO-1. Contrast qid:105980, which asks only for its regional name.
Features of primitive subsistence agriculture: the pattern's defining characteristics, LO-1.
Names jhumming, the north-eastern term for slash and burn. Regional nomenclature, so C-2.1; the classification of the practice itself is at qid:105978.
Intensive subsistence farming as labour-intensive farming: the pattern's defining feature, LO-1.
Why agricultural land is under such pressure: too large a share of the workforce on too little land, which is exactly the imbalance LO-12 asks about and its consequence for rural incomes.

Identifies commercial farming from its modern-input package: classification of a farming pattern, LO-1. Not C-2.3-LO-10, which would require the Green Revolution's gains and costs to be weighed rather than its inputs listed.
Rice as commercial in Punjab and subsistence in Odisha: the same crop under two patterns, which is LO-1's classification applied regionally.
Characteristics of plantation farming: the pattern's defining features, LO-1.
Names the important plantation crops: the major-crop half of LO-1.
The state known for tea: crop-to-state matching, LO-1.
Count of India's cropping seasons: the cropping calendar, LO-1.
When rabi crops are harvested: the cropping calendar, LO-1.
Identifies the rabi crops: season-to-crop matching, LO-1.
The state known for rabi crops: season-and-region matching, LO-1.
Winter precipitation from western temperate cyclones as the key to rabi success: the climatic basis of a cropping season, LO-1.
Which states succeeded in the Green Revolution is LO-10's 'uneven spread' clause. Not C-2.1-LO-2, which assesses reforms in general rather than this one's geography.
When kharif crops are harvested: the cropping calendar, LO-1.
Names a kharif crop: season-to-crop matching, LO-1.
Names a wheat-growing region: crop geography, LO-1.
Names a zaid crop: season-to-crop matching for the third season, LO-1.
Names a rice-growing region: crop geography, LO-1.
Three paddy crops a year in Assam, West Bengal and Odisha: multiple cropping, which is a cropping pattern, LO-1.
Duplicate of qid:105997; names a zaid crop, LO-1.
Sugarcane's growing period: a major crop's requirements, LO-1.
India's rank among rice producers: production data for a major crop, LO-1.
Rice's rainfall requirement: a growing condition, LO-1.

Rice grown in low-rainfall Punjab, Haryana, western UP and Rajasthan only because of irrigation. That is a technological reform in Indian agriculture, LO-2. LO-10 would fit an item weighing the Green Revolution's costs, such as groundwater depletion, which this one does not raise.
Weather conditions favourable to wheat: growing requirements, LO-1.
Wheat's 50-75 cm evenly distributed rainfall requirement: the same growing condition as qid:105954 in statement form, LO-1.
The two wheat-growing zones: crop geography, duplicate target of qid:105953.
Which crops count as millets: crop classification, LO-1.
What millets are nutritionally rich in: crop characteristics, LO-1.
Jowar's rank among food crops: production data for a major crop, LO-1.
Jowar as a rain-fed crop needing little irrigation: growing conditions, LO-1.
Names a major jowar state: crop-to-state matching, LO-1.
The soil bajra suits: a growing condition of a major crop, LO-1.
The crop serving as both food and fodder: crop use within the major-crop classification, LO-1.
India's rank as producer and consumer of pulses: production data, LO-1.
The crop requiring manual labour from sowing to harvest: a labour characteristic of a major crop, LO-1.
Names a major banana state: crop-to-state matching, LO-1.
Where rubber is grown: crop geography, LO-1.
Silk as the fibre from silkworm cocoons: the fibre-crop classification, LO-1. Contrast qid:105965, which asks for the name of the rearing process.
Jute as the golden fibre: duplicate target of qid:105966, LO-1.
Names a major jute state: crop-to-state matching, LO-1.
India's rank in fruit and vegetable production: production data for horticultural crops, LO-1.
